subject: Computer Science

assessmentTargets.concept: State the definition of the Longest Common Prefix problem, including input type and required output.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: You're given a bunch of strings, and what you need to return is the prefix, which is common amongst all of them.

assessmentTargets.concept: Explain why the length of the smallest string bounds the maximum possible common prefix length.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: the first thing you would need to find out is what is the length of the smallest string? Because the longest common prefix cannot be larger than the smallest string.
assessmentTargets.evidenceSpan: Segment 2 discussion of smallest string length

assessmentTargets.concept: Describe how a hash set is used to determine whether a character at a given index is common to all strings.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: We add h to it. h gets added. I add one more h. What does set guarantee? No duplicates. So the second h does not add. If the size of the set is one, you know this character has occurred in all strings.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Summarize the role of the hash set.

assessmentTargets.concept: Trace the algorithm: outer loop over character positions up to the smallest length, inner loop over each string, and break when a mismatch occurs.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: The outer loop is number of characters you want to process. The inner loop is one character at a time of all the three strings... If the size is not one, we break out of each loop.
assessmentTargets.evidenceSpan: Segment 3 walkthrough of loops and break condition
assessmentTargets.instruction: Provide a step‑by‑step trace for a sample input.

assessmentTargets.concept: Compare hash‑set based approach with binary‑search and built‑in string API approaches in terms of time efficiency, readability, and maintainability.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: ...talk about using hash set, then talk about using hash map, and then look at how we can do this using binary search using the built‑in strings API... also consider readability and maintenance.

reserveTargets.concept: Identify the output when no common prefix exists among the strings.
reserveTargets.supportingEvidence: Then obviously the output would be empty string because there is no prefix which is common amongst all the three strings.
reserveTargets.instruction: State the expected result for this case.

reserveTargets.concept: Explain why processing beyond the smallest string length can cause array index out‑of‑bounds errors.
reserveTargets.supportingEvidence: there is no point processing all the characters of every string because you might end up getting into array index out of bounds if you're not very careful about it.

reserveTargets.concept: Discuss why clean, readable code is emphasized for long‑term maintenance.
reserveTargets.supportingEvidence: code has to be maintained. If a code is easy to maintain, then it has a much longer shelf life than a code which is gobbled up.
